pattern.name: url_parsing
pattern.description: Extracting owner and repo name from git origin remote URL
pattern.explanation: Use regex or string splitting to extract `{owner}` and `{repo}` reliably from `git config --get remote.origin.url`.

pattern.name: label_retrieval_and_semantic_matching
pattern.description: Retrieve existing repo labels once per session and match semantically
pattern.code: 1. When preparing first issue draft of session: - Call list_issues or repo label query to get existing repository labels. - Cache label list in memory for the duration of the session. 2. Match issue type semantically: - Bug -> match against "bug", "type: bug", "defect", "kind/bug", etc. - Feature/Enhancement -> match against "enhancement", "feature", "type: feature", etc. - Task/Chore -> match against "task", "chore", "refactor", etc. 3. Outcome: - If match found -> propose matched label in draft presented at Gate #1. - If no reasonable match -> propose no label (never create a new repo label).
pattern.explanation: Reuses existing repo taxonomy without polluting the repository with new labels.

pattern.name: type_aware_issue_templates
pattern.description: Standard GitHub public issue templates by issue type (Excludes internal Acceptance Criteria)
pattern.code:
## Summary [Clear summary of bug]
## Steps to Reproduce 1. [Step one] 2. [Step two]
## Expected Behavior [What should happen]
## Actual Behavior [What actually happens]
## Summary [Clear summary of feature or task]
## Motivation & Context [Why this is needed / context]
## Proposed Implementation / Desired Behavior [What should be implemented or changed]

pattern.name: internal_acceptance_criteria_template
pattern.description: Private scratchpad checklist used strictly by Roo for validation (Never pushed to GitHub)

pattern.name: lazy_stakeholder_assignment_and_fallback
pattern.description: Lazy resolution and assignment workflow when issue is left open without fix
pattern.code: 1. Batch local config queries (e.g., git config --get user.email). 2. Search GitHub for account ({email}+in:email). 3. If search returns matching login -> assign that user. 4. If email is unset OR search returns 0 matches -> Unified Fallback: - Assign default repo owner (if known), OR - Prompt user via ask_followup_question: "Could not find a GitHub user for this email. Would you like to assign a specific GitHub user?"
pattern.explanation: Defer identity search until assignment is required. Apply a single consistent fallback whether email is missing or lookup finds zero results.

pattern.name: manual_issue_closure_template
pattern.description: Formalized workflow for manual issue closure (Not Planned / Duplicate)
pattern.code: 1. Identify closure category: - "not planned": reason = "not_planned", comment explaining rationale. - "duplicate": reason = "not_planned", comment referencing canonical issue (e.g., "Duplicate of #10"), apply duplicate label if available. 2. Present proposed closure draft to user: - State reason, any label modification, and exact comment text. - Prompt via ask_followup_question: ["Approve and close issue", "Keep issue open", "Modify closing comment"]. 3. Halt execution until user response (Strict turn separation). 4. Upon approval in subsequent turn: - Post closing comment via add_issue_comment. - Update issue status to closed (with state_reason: "not_planned" and label if applicable).
pattern.explanation: Ensures all non-merge issue closures are explicit, transparent, and user-approved with explanatory comments.

pattern.name: blanket_destructive_action_confirmation
pattern.description: Blanket confirmation protocol for terminal or destructive actions
pattern.code: 1. Any terminal/destructive operation (deleting local/remote branch, closing issue, deleting comment): - Identify the exact target entity (e.g., branch name `issue-5-old-fix`). - Present specific proposal to user via ask_followup_question. 2. Even if the user gave a broad command ("clean up stale branches"): - Do NOT execute batch deletions automatically. - List the specific targets to be deleted and ask for explicit confirmation in a subsequent turn.
pattern.explanation: Protects against irreversible data loss and ensures user oversight for all destructive actions.

pattern.name: pr_merge_and_error_handling
pattern.description: Attempting PR merge directly with graceful failure handling
pattern.code: 1. Prompt user: "Merge PR now and clean up workspace" vs "Leave PR open for maintainer review". 2. If user chooses merge: - Call merge_pull_request(merge_method='squash') - If success: report success, proceed to workspace restoration and delete feature branch. - If failure: report actual error plainly, do not retry automatically, proceed to workspace restoration (git checkout main && git pull), and preserve remote branch.
pattern.explanation: Never pre-evaluate permissions. Handle any merge failure as a normal outcome and restore local workspace.
